changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 2 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6310-designer-formula-key-retired.md`

- names `FieldDesigner.tsx` → `packages/plugin-designer/src/FieldDesigner.tsx` — edited by this change

  > objectui#6043 retired the Field Designer's formula-expression textarea, which was the key's only call site (`FieldDesigner.tsx`, the `{ name: 'formula', label: t('appDesigner.fieldDesigner.formula') }` field descriptor). The value outlived it in eleven places: `DESIGNER_DEFAULT_TRANSLATIONS` in `packages/plugin-designer/src/hooks/useDesignerTranslation.ts`, and the `appDesigner > fieldDesigner > formula` leaf of `packages/i18n/src/locales/{en,de,es,fr,pt,ru,ja,ko,zh,ar}.ts`.

### `.changeset/8568-retire-dollar-dialect-lowercase-aliases.md`

- names `packages/data-objectstack/README.md` → `packages/data-objectstack/README.md` — edited by this change

  > `packages/data-objectstack/README.md`'s operator tables follow the implementation, as does the reconciliation test that holds them to it.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `58da8aeca` (merge-base with origin/main): 13 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1856 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2468 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36792508020)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `54c202695f20825e08ee81633a2fa909e7027a90`
Local-runs: none

Reviewed against the card objectui#11253 (body and all four comments: triage `5917874517`, the serial note `5919350282`, the claim `5920025935`, the dev report `5921397439`), PR objectui#11287 (body, 14-file list, net diff at the merge-base `7d074baaec` against `main`), the 42 check-runs on the head, the maintainer's ruling A on objectstack#20827 (`5910124148`), and objectstack `origin/main` and the `@objectstack/spec@17.5.0` tag read-only for the ADR-0078 rule the guard cites.

**Gate verdicts on the head.** 27 `success`, 3 `skipped` (the coverage shards and dependabot), **1 `failure`: `Doc Snippet Type Check`**, and 11 `in_progress`, NOT concluded: `Lint`, `Spec Main Shape Gate`, `Type Check`, and `Test (shard 1/8)` through `Test (shard 8/8)`. The same `Doc Snippet Type Check` is `success` on the PR base `1b30c0fe08` (two runs) and on the merge-base `7d074baaec` (one `success`, one `cancelled`), so the failure enters with this diff. Its job's steps 1 to 8 passed (install, derive the build filter, build, template-literal census) and step 9, "Compile documentation snippets against the built types", is the failure; the job log itself sits on a blob host the proxy denies, so the cause below is read off the gate's stated rule and the diff, not off the log.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The narrowing, and it is one.** `assertObjectMetadataWritable('object', …)` — and so `MetadataClient.save('object', …)`, `importObjectDraft` and `MetadataService`, the three doors `check:metadata-write-doors` derives (CI: `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and the door pin `metadata-client.objectWriteGuard.test.ts` on the head) — now throws before any request when a `select` / `radio` carries neither a non-empty `options` array nor a `picklist` string. `options` absent, `[]`, `null` and non-array are each refused and the message says which state it saw, naming the field and the door. **Right.** One seam, no second module, no writer list: the diff adds one predicate and one throw to the existing loop; the claim's ⛔ holds.
2. **The predicate is the ruling's "neither `options` nor `picklist`", read right.** `hasOptionSource` is "`Array.isArray(options)` with a positive `length`, or `typeof picklist === 'string'`", which is objectstack `main`'s `functional-completeness.ts` line 193 verbatim (`hasEntries(def.options) || typeof def.picklist === 'string'`, with `hasEntries` the non-empty-array test). `options: []` as no source is the contract's own reading at BOTH ends: the installed 17.5.0 rule is `!hasEntries(def.options)` (its line 190) and `main`'s `FieldSchema` comment says "Neither, on a single-choice type, stays the error-severity `FIELD_CHOICE_WITHOUT_OPTIONS` finding … whose prescription names both". A `picklist` string always passing is the other half of "neither"; the guard is not a revalidation, so the server judges the name (and, on `main`, refuses `picklist` together with a declared `options`, `[]` included — the guard's "with or without an empty list" pin describes the guard only, and that is the right division). **Right**, with one precision the dev stated and I confirm at the tag: the installed 17.5.0 rule has NO `picklist` half at all, and 17.5.0's `FieldSchema` is a `strictObject` without a `picklist` key, so the `picklist` arm is taken from `main` ahead of the installed spec; until objectui's pin moves, a `picklist`-bearing field is a server 422 that the surfaces already hold as a server refusal. That is the ruling's word, not an invention.
3. **`CHOICE_TYPES_REQUIRING_OPTIONS = ['select', 'radio']` is derived from the installed spec and pinned.** `@objectstack/spec@17.5.0`'s `kernel/index.ts` re-exports `functional-completeness`, whose `DEAD_WITHOUT_OPTIONS_ERROR` is exactly `{select, radio}` with `checkboxes` at `warning`; the derivation pin filters `FieldType.options` through `checkFieldCompleteness` at `error` severity and asserts equality, with the non-trivial-probe control and the `checkboxes`-is-warning control. The "cut to `['select']`" ablation the dev reports is consistent with that pin. **Right.**
4. **The counter-cases hold the guard to its ruling.** `multiselect` / `checkboxes` / `tags` without options pass (pinned); every non-`object` metadata type is a no-op (pinned); the array `fields` shape the Studio page PUTs is read (pinned). **Right.**
5. **The docblock's contract is now honest, per rule.** The old "cannot dead-bolt anything the server would have taken" is split: the relationship rule keeps it (a 422 one layer down), the choice rule states it is deliberately AHEAD of the server, quotes ruling A's execution parameter (2), and the derivation file's "installed server still ACCEPTS" block measures that claim on every run and says in its own comment what to do when it turns red (rewrite the paragraph into the relationship form, flip the block to a refusal at `options`). The PR's Acceptance notes name the carrier (the spec-bump PR). **Right**, and the flip is stated where it will be read.
6. **The dead-bolt risk on the two Studio-family surfaces: pinned on the real surfaces, and cleared on screen.** Studio Data pillar: `doSave`'s catch is `setError(formatMetadataError(e))` and the banner at `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` line 2397 shows it; `useDraftAutoSave` refuses to resend the same `snapKey` (`lastAttemptRef`), so a held save is not re-attempted until the next edit, which re-arms it. The pin mounts the real `DataPillar` with a real `MetadataClient` and only `fetch` stubbed, adds a field, types it `select` / `radio`, outlasts the debounce, reads the wire (no PUT with a choice and no option source), reads the banner (names the field, says "no options"), then types one option and reads the next PUT carrying it. The stored-empty-`select` case is measured too: an unrelated label edit is held, the banner names the STORED field, one option in that field's own inspector sends ONE PUT carrying both edits, so nothing held is lost. metadata-admin: the guard's `Error` has no `status` and no error code, so `doSave` lands in the plain `setError(err.message)` branch, `setIssues([])`, and `refusalBlocking` stays unarmed; the autosave effect skips a payload equal to `lastAutoSaveSnapshotRef` ("so a validation failure doesn't loop on the same payload"), so each later edit re-runs the guard locally and re-shows the banner — no hammering, no request. The pin mounts the real `MetadataResourceEditPage` with `register-builtins`, adds `Picklist` / `Radio` from the palette (the `options: []` seed), and measures the same three things. **Right**: "a held autosave shows why it is held" is met on both, and both surfaces are unchanged for a measured reason. One asymmetry to know: the stored-field unrelated-edit case is pinned on Studio only; metadata-admin's pin covers the palette-added case. The seam and the banner path are the same, so I do not require a second pin.
7. **plugin-designer's stored option-less field: a redirect, not an in-page clear — an Acceptance note, not blocking.** Read at the head: `DESIGNER_FIELD_TYPES` (`packages/types/src/designer.ts`) holds `select` and not `radio`, as the dev says. A stored `select` with no options is designable there: the drawer offers its own type (the `editingType` exception), has no options editor, so the author's in-page remedies are to retype it to a non-choice type or remove it — a real clearing path, and it loses nothing since there were no options. A stored `radio` with no options is in the preserved half (`partitionStoredFields`), carried through unedited, so ANY save from `MetadataFieldsPage` (an edit to a different field) is now refused by name in the page's own error banner, and the page's remedies do not reach it; the preserved section's text is "Use metadata-admin to change them." So a plugin-designer author cannot clear that refusal without leaving the page. I judge it acceptable and note-worthy, not blocking: (a) it is the exact shape of the accepted target-less `master_detail` precedent on the same page, which the relationship rule already holds the same way; (b) ruling A's execution parameter (1) makes the same PUT a server refusal once the door closes ("new writes refused, stored rows read through the legacy path and named") — the guard changes WHEN that page is held, not WHETHER; (c) triage chose the one-seam guard over create-with-options knowing plugin-designer has no options editor. What is thin: the plugin-designer refusal of a stored option-less `radio` is a reading in the report, not a pin (the P1 census fixture that used to carry one now gives it an option, so no test shows the page held by name), and the guard's message names two remedies ("Add an option, or change the field to a non-choice type") that page cannot perform for a preserved field. **Acceptance note on the card**; fileable at low priority as a `finding` (a pin on `MetadataFieldsPage` for the held stored `radio`, and that page's banner pointing at metadata-admin when the named field is a preserved one). Not a dead-bolt the ruling does not intend.
8. **plugin-designer hides the choice types except the edited field's own stored type.** `drawerOffersType` hides every member of `CHOICE_TYPES_REQUIRING_OPTIONS` from the drawer's type picker for a new field and for retyping a non-choice field, keeps a field's own stored type so an existing picklist round-trips with its options, and leaves the list's type FILTER whole. Pinned (four cases, absence paired with presence in each reading). That is triage's "hide the choice types until it has an options editor": the drawer creates no choice, and the exception is what stops the hide from stripping the type off fields that already are one. **Right.** `radio` was never in the drawer's vocabulary, so nothing to hide there.
9. **The two fixture edits are fixtures, not pins of changed behaviour.** `MetadataFieldsPage.saveEnvelope` (objectui#4546, S0 to S4) measures that the PUT body is the object body and not the response envelope; `stage` is scenery. `MetadataFieldsPage.storedTypePreserved` (objectui#8060, P1 census, P3, P6) measures that a stored type survives an edit to a different field; the choice members gain one option the way `master_detail` already got a `reference`. None asserted "an option-less choice is accepted"; they assumed it. **Right** — with the observation in item 7 that the P1 census fixture was the one place a stored option-less `radio` rode through this page, and no new pin replaces that observation with the refusal.
10. **The public surface.** One new export, `CHOICE_TYPES_REQUIRING_OPTIONS`, from `@object-ui/data-objectstack`'s index, beside `RELATIONSHIP_TYPES_REQUIRING_REFERENCE`, documented in the README's guard section and the changeset, consumed by `FieldDesigner` so plugin-designer hides exactly the guard's set rather than a remembered list; `README Export Check` is `success` on the head. **Right.**
11. **The one wrong derived judgment: the README's new snippet, and the gate that caught it.** The diff's only documentation-fence change is the second `ts` fence in `packages/data-objectstack/README.md`'s "Object-Metadata Write Guard" section: `await client.save('object', 'deal', { … options: [] … })`. `scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs` compiles EVERY `ts` fence of a covered document (every `packages/NAME/README.md` is covered by default) in ISOLATION as its own module, with `export {}` appended so a block "cannot see another block's globals" — modelling the reader who copies one block. The new fence declares no `client` and imports nothing; the `const client = new MetadataClient(…)` it relies on lives in the sibling fence above it. Under the gate's own rule that is an undeclared name in a block that is neither self-contained nor declared a fragment with the gate's `doc-snippet: fragment` marker line (the README already uses that marker once, at its line 881, for a signature excerpt). The dev's gate roster ran `check:doc-fences`, `docs:check-links` and `check:readme-exports`, but not `check:doc-snippets`, which is the gate that went red.
